body.statement:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) lie in the relative interior of a fixed structural support stratum on which the observed-cell factor map in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\) has locally constant rank \(k_P\).  For the actual support \(\mathcal S_P\), construct \(A_P\), \(W_P\), and \(S_P=W_P^{-1}A_P\) as in that definition.  Then
\[
 \mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(S_P),
 \qquad S_P^\top W_PS_P=A_P^\top W_P^{-1}A_P\succ0.
\]
For \(G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}=(G_{p,\ell}(s))_{s\in\mathcal S_P}\), the constrained canonical gradient is computable coordinatewise by
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}
 =S_P(S_P^\top W_PS_P)^{-1}S_P^\top W_PG_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}.
\]
The target is \(\theta=\Phi(p)\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)^\top\}\) is the pointwise covariance lower bound among mean-zero influence vectors representing the derivative of \(\theta\) along \(\mathcal T_P\).  Moreover, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\),
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.
\]
Consequently the constrained bound is strictly smaller than the saturated bound in direction \(a\) exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\).  This result neither asserts existence of an attaining restricted-model estimator nor establishes uniform constrained efficiency over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\).
body.justification: The explicit latent-mixture product Jacobian turns the pointwise restricted tangent calculation into an evaluable weighted projection on regular fixed-support strata.
body.gap: The broad class neither imposes the date-\(4\) common kernel nor buffers restricted Jacobian rank or support changes, and no attaining restricted estimator is constructed.
body.consumer: A specified fifth-date likelihood can compute the pointwise influence-function lower bound from its cell Jacobian; the broad guarded bands remain the proved inferential procedure.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\) satisfying the stated fixed-support and constant-rank conditions.  Put \(m_P=|\mathcal S_P|\), enumerate \(\mathcal S_P\), and identify a function on \(\mathcal S_P\) with its vector of cell values.  Since \(P\) is in the relative interior of this stratum, \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S_P\).  Hence \(W_P\) is positive definite and \(W_P^{-1}\) used in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\) exists.

We first verify that the construction in that definition is the observed-law parameterization of the restricted model.  Conditional on \((D=d,Z=j)\), consistency and no anticipation identify the observed variables through date \(2\) with the corresponding potential path.  The type-conditional first-order Markov property therefore gives, for every legal cell \(s=(d,x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(O=s)
 &=P(D=d)\sum_{j=1}^2P(Z=j\mid D=d)
       P(X_0=x_0\mid Z=j,D=d)\\
 &\quad\times P(X_1=x_1\mid X_0=x_0,Z=j,D=d)
       P(X_2=x_2\mid X_1=x_1,Z=j,D=d)\\
 &\quad\times P(X_3=x_3\mid X_2=x_2,Z=j,D=d)
       P(X_4=x_4\mid X_3=x_3,Z=j,D=d).
\end{aligned}                                           \tag{1}
\]
The common date-\(2\) transition assumption makes the third transition factor in \((1)\) equal to \(Q_j[x_1,x_2]\).  In the control cohort, the common first-post untreated transition and common date-\(4\) untreated transition make the last two factors \(U_j[x_2,x_3]\) and \(L_j[x_3,x_4]\).  In the treated cohort, they are the factual treated kernels \(V_j[x_2,x_3]\) and \(T_{4,j}^1[x_3,x_4]\).  Absorption fixes the exit rows and forbids precisely the coordinates outside \(\mathcal G\).  Thus \((1)\) is exactly the polynomial cell map \(q(\beta)\) in \(\text{def:efficiency-handle}\).  Conversely, its simplex constraints, common-coordinate restrictions, and absorbing rows generate the observed marginal of a type-conditional Markov law on this fixed stratum; observationally null cross-potential couplings do not change any score in \(L_2(P)\).

Let \(B_P=Dq(\beta_P)\) be the full Jacobian before redundant columns are removed.  Each column sums to zero because \(\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_P}q_s(\beta)=1\).  If \(\varepsilon\mapsto\beta(\varepsilon)\) is a differentiable restricted submodel through \(\beta_P\) with velocity \(v\), differentiation gives
\[
 \dot q=B_Pv,
 \qquad
 h(s)=\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}
       \log q_s\{\beta(\varepsilon)\}\right|_{\varepsilon=0}
       =\frac{(B_Pv)_s}{p_s}.                            \tag{2}
\]
Thus every restricted score belongs to \(\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}B_P)\).  Conversely, the relative-interior condition permits sufficiently small two-sided perturbations in every free chart direction.  Hence every column of \(W_P^{-1}B_P\), and therefore every linear combination of those columns, is a restricted score.  By construction, \(A_P\) has independent columns spanning \(\operatorname{col}(B_P)\).  Equation \((2)\) consequently proves
\[
 \mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}B_P)
             =\operatorname{col}(W_P^{-1}A_P)
             =\operatorname{col}(S_P).                  \tag{3}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathbf 1_{m_P}^\top W_PS_P=\mathbf 1_{m_P}^\top A_P=0\), so every vector in \((3)\) has mean zero under \(P\).  The space in \((3)\) is finite dimensional and hence closed.  Also, for every nonzero \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_P}\),
\[
 c^\top S_P^\top W_PS_Pc
 =(A_Pc)^\top W_P^{-1}(A_Pc)>0,                         \tag{4}
\]
because \(W_P^{-1}\succ0\) and \(A_P\) has full column rank.  This proves both the asserted information-matrix identity and the inverse condition used below.

By \(\text{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\), the causal target equals the observed-law functional \(\theta=\Phi(p)\) throughout the compatible fiber.  By \(\text{thm:analytic-gradient}\), for each coordinate \(\ell\) and every saturated score \(h\), and hence for every \(h\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
 \dot\theta_{P,\ell}[h]
 =E_P\{G_{p,\ell}(O)h(O)\}
 =(G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P})^\top W_Ph.                \tag{5}
\]
The \(W_P\)-orthogonal projection of a vector \(g\in\mathbb R^{m_P}\) onto \(\operatorname{col}(S_P)\) is found by minimizing
\[
 \min_{b\in\mathbb R^{k_P}}(g-S_Pb)^\top W_P(g-S_Pb).  \tag{6}
\]
Differentiating \((6)\) gives the normal equation
\[
 S_P^\top W_PS_Pb=S_P^\top W_Pg.                        \tag{7}
\]
The coefficient matrix in \((7)\) is invertible by \((4)\).  Substituting \(g=G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}\) therefore yields
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal T_P}G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P}
 =S_P(S_P^\top W_PS_P)^{-1}S_P^\top W_P
  G_{p,\ell}^{\mathcal S_P},                            \tag{8}
\]
which is the promised finite, evaluable formula.  Equations \((5)\) and \((8)\) show that
\[
 E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}(O)h(O)\}
 =\dot\theta_{P,\ell}[h]
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal T_P.               \tag{9}
\]
If another element of \(\mathcal T_P\) represents the same derivative, its difference from \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_P\) and is orthogonal to \(\mathcal T_P\), so it is zero.  Thus \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\) is the constrained canonical gradient.

It remains to establish the lower bound and its comparison with the saturated bound.  Fix \(a\in\mathbb R^9\), and let \(\varphi_a\in L_2^0(P)\) be any scalar influence function representing the derivative of \(a^\top\theta\) along every \(h\in\mathcal T_P\).  By \((9)\),
\[
 E_P[\{\varphi_a(O)-a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\}h(O)]=0
 \quad(h\in\mathcal T_P).                              \tag{10}
\]
Since \(a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\in\mathcal T_P\), Pythagoras and \((10)\) give
\[
 E_P\{\varphi_a(O)^2\}
 =a^\top V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)a
  +\|\varphi_a-a^\top\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\|_{L_2(P)}^2
 \ge a^\top V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)a.                      \tag{11}
\]
This proves the stated pointwise covariance lower bound without asserting that an estimator attaining it exists.

Finally set \(R_\ell=(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})G_{p,\ell}\).  Projection orthogonality gives
\[
 \Sigma_{\ell r}(p)
 =E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}(O)
        \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,r}(O)\}+E_P\{R_\ell(O)R_r(O)\}. \tag{12}
\]
Multiplying \((12)\) by \(a_\ell a_r\) and summing proves
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.      \tag{13}
\]
The right side of \((13)\) is positive exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\), proving the strictness criterion.  The construction is pointwise on a fixed relative-interior constant-rank stratum.  The class \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\) neither imposes the date-\(4\) restriction nor buffers the rank of \(A_P\) or changes of \(\mathcal S_P\); therefore no uniform constrained-efficiency conclusion follows.
